findings.evidence: "make a meme about bugs everywhere in our release" exemplifies the positive queries: all explicitly name memes, greentext, memegen.link or a template. None tests the description's implicit reaction-image or image-URL captioning triggers, and none supplies a custom background URL.
findings.fix: Replace two explicit positives with realistic implicit requests: a contextual Slack comparison-image request without the word 'meme', and a request to caption a supplied public image URL at specified dimensions. Keep the balanced positive/negative set and existing near-miss negatives.

findings.evidence: "No Python? Send POST https://api.memegen.link/images with JSON {\"template_id\": \"<id>\", \"text\": [\"<top>\", \"<bottom>\"]}" omits the selected background and rendering options. Following this fallback for the advertised custom-image branch loses the user's background instead of producing the requested image.
findings.fix: Route no-Python requests through the documented hand-built URL procedure, preserving one path segment per caption and all selected query parameters. Explicitly require the percent-encoded background parameter for custom images and preserve width, height, layout, font and style when supplied.
